Record a decision on one possible-duplicate pair shown on contact <id> (identity rules v2; needs contacts:edit on BOTH records). --decision is required and must be exactly one of not_sure (keep both records visible; the pair stays listed), different (different people: never shown again, FINAL) or merge (record that the pair is ALREADY merged; this command never merges: run `contacts merge` first, else 409 not_merged). Answers { id, status, decidedAt, previousMembershipRevision, membershipRevision, total }: membershipRevision and total are the contact's proposals list AFTER the decision (the same digest and count `list-contact` answers), previousMembershipRevision the digest just BEFORE the write (equal on an idempotent repeat); keep loaded pages only when previousMembershipRevision equals the revision you hold, otherwise read page one again. Refusals (409 already_decided / not_merged, 403 other_record_not_editable, 404, 400) exit non-zero with the API's message and code. List the possible duplicates of contact <id> (identity rules v2; read-only, contacts:view): { proposals, heldIdentifiers, total, nextCursor, membershipRevision, heldIdentifiersTotal, heldIdentifiersNextCursor, heldIdentifiersMembershipRevision }. Each proposal has id (the <proposalId> for `decide-contact`), status (open | not_sure), rule, raisedHere and `other` { id, name, createdAt, visible, editable }; a record you cannot view is "a contact you cannot view" with no id. heldIdentifiers are emails or phones this record was not given because another record owns them (value-free). Both lists are keyset paged, newest first: --cursor / --limit (1-100, default 50) page the proposals, --held-cursor / --held-limit (1-100, default 20) the held identifiers; total and heldIdentifiersTotal count every line (all pages); pass nextCursor / heldIdentifiersNextCursor back unchanged (null on the last page). membershipRevision and heldIdentifiersMembershipRevision are opaque digests of each list: when a later page answers another revision than page one, discard it and read page one again. A cursor this list did not issue is a 400 invalid_cursor. There is no --all: the two lists page separately under the revision rule.

It prints { columns: [{ stageId, limit, deals }], meta: { board_snapshot: true } } (under data): columns in the order named, each column's deals exactly what --stage <stageId> --per-page <limit> rows-only answers (same filters, order and projection), no totals; deals.length equal to limit means the column may hold more. 1-50 live stages of the pipeline, no stage twice, limit a whole number 1-1000 (default --per-page, itself default 50), at most 5000 rows in total. Refused before any request (usage error): --page (even 1: a snapshot is always page one), --stage, --all, every other deals list filter (the snapshot forwards only --pipeline, --status, --assigned-to, --sort, --order and --per-page), --board-columns without --board-snapshot, a missing --pipeline or --board-columns, --data-source local, and a --board-columns value the server would refuse. A snapshot is always read live (never the response cache, never written into the local store). 503 (nothing was changed; retried by the client, then the error carries the code and retryAfter): board_snapshot_busy (--board-snapshot only: the one snapshot could not finish in its budget; read the columns one by one with --stage, or retry) and gate_busy (any deals list call, snapshot or not: the access check could not finish in time; retry after Retry-After).

List the duplicate proposals one import raised on the records it created (the import results section "Created, similar record exists"; read-only, contacts:view): one row per proposal, every status (open | not_sure | different | merged; a merged pair reads merged), oldest first. Answers { rows, meta: { page, per_page, total } } (total counts every row of the import). Each row: proposalId, status, rowNum (the import file's row number), createdAt, decidedAt, decidedByName, newRecord (the record the import created), similar (the existing record it may duplicate), matchedOn (kinds only, such as phone or phone + company, never a value), keptName; newRecord and similar are { id, name, visible, editable, live }. A record you cannot view has no id and the name "A contact you cannot view". Decide a row with `contacts duplicate-proposals decide-contact <newRecord.id> <proposalId> --decision ...` (contacts:edit on both records). An owner, admin or view-all key reads any import of the account, any other key only the imports its user ran (404 otherwise). Paged with --page (1-100000, default 1) and --per-page (1-100, default 50); there is no --all.

Use this command for a go/no-go verdict on exactly one smart list, tag, or contact: per contact, phone present and mappable, Twilio-verified line type, Twilio validity, and the contact's SMS DNC status from GET /contacts/dnc-status. Local mirror filters are applied before --limit; live list reads paginate up to --limit, while repeatable live tags are merged and de-duplicated before --limit. An empty scope is a clean 0-checked answer. Exits 0 on go (or an empty scope), 2 on no_go or a usage error, 3 when --contact does not exist, 4 when DNC access is unauthorized (needs the 'communications' view scope), and 5 when the result is inconclusive (a capped, short or failed audience read, or a DNC answer that is missing, truncated or omits a contact). tests.output_sample:
Sync data from the API into a local SQLite database. Supports resumable
incremental sync (only fetches new data since last sync) and full resync.
Once synced, use the 'search' command for instant full-text search.

Exit codes & warnings:
  Resources the API denies access to (HTTP 403, or HTTP 400 with an
  access-policy body) are reported as warnings rather than failing the
  run. In --json mode each is emitted as a {"event":"sync_warning",...}
  line carrying status, reason, and message fields, and a final
  {"event":"sync_summary",...} aggregates the run.

  Exit 0 when at least one resource synced and no resource flagged in
  the spec as critical (x-critical: true) failed; non-critical failures
  emit {"event":"sync_warning","reason":"exit_policy_default_changed",
  ...} so callers can detect that a partial failure was tolerated. Pass
  --strict to exit non-zero on any per-resource failure. Exit is always
  non-zero when every selected resource failed, regardless of --strict.

Resource scoping:
  --resources runs the named top-level resources, plus any parent-keyed
  dependent whose own name is listed OR whose parent table is listed.
  Naming a parent therefore cascades to its dependents (so "sync this
  parent and its children" works without listing every nested resource
  by hand). There is no flag today to suppress the cascade for a named
